title: Kyler Murray Talks Vikings Ascending Offense, Continued Improvement, Working with Kevin O'Connell
headline: Kyler Murray (not the coach) says the offense is ascending, his comfort with Kevin O'Connell is growing fast, and the team is getting injured players back before Week 7 at Indianapolis.
summary: This is a player availability, not a head coach press conference, so the statements below are Kyler Murray's. He said the week off was a little too long, but useful for the unit to get some banged-up players back, and he wanted to stay sharp by completing passes. Murray described the offense as ascending and said the recent stretch has been good, though he wants more touchdowns in the end zone and fewer costly turnovers, especially against better opponents. He said players felt rejuvenated coming back from the bye, and that the team is close-knit. Asked about Jordan Mason and Jordan Addison having only shared three snaps due to injuries, he avoided dwelling on it, said there were no excuses, and said the team is happy to have everybody back at full strength. He said he is having more fun as the season goes on, is getting more comfortable with the offense and with O'Connell, and calls the progress in their relationship 'night and day' thanks to time spent together. He acknowledged growing pains and that the team wanted a faster start, but said they understand the standard the offense is held to.

signals.claim: Feels increasingly comfortable running the offense and building rapport with O'Connell and the skill players
signals.note: Comfort with the system and receivers usually shows up as better accuracy and decision-making, which supports QB and pass-game production.
signals.quote: I definitely feel more comfortable, you know, as I take each snap

topics.detail: Murray says the offense is ascending but wants to finish drives with touchdowns and cut down on turnovers, which were costly in recent games.
The bye let some injured players return to practice; Murray did not name them, and the Mason and Addison injury history was raised but not detailed.
Murray credits time spent with Kevin O'Connell for rapid improvement and says the growing pains were expected.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 22, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley's return is still undetermined; Sirianni says it depends on how the week progresses, and Zach Ertz has been impressing in practice.
summary: Sirianni called Saquon Barkley a phenomenal player and captain, and said getting him back would be huge, but he would not commit to a timeline and said they will see where things stand as the week goes on. He said a run game that converts on third down keeps the play-action passing game working, and that the backs in the room have stepped up during injuries. On Jalen Hurts, he declined to discuss his timetable or the NFLPA's call for an investigation, saying he cares deeply about Hurts's well-being and that it is fluid. He declined to discuss the reported $250,000 fine or his conversations with the league and referees association. He praised Tanner McKee's intelligence and toughness and said McKee should keep rising, with every rep counting. On the offense, he said the staff must balance a system with attacking defenses using players' strengths, and that players matter more than plays. He acknowledged the team has lost four straight games and that it needs to get back on track. He praised Zach Ertz's practices and said he has had great reps with the first team and useful looks as a scout-team player. On the Cowboys, he said Christian Parker's familiarity with the Eagles is limited to his role in the building, since he was not in offensive meetings, and that film study is the main way to beat him.

injuries.detail: Return is uncertain; Sirianni said they'll see where he is as the week progresses and he was looking forward to seeing him at practice.
Sirianni would not discuss his recovery or timetable, saying it is fluid and that everyone's recovery differs. He is not around the team daily.
